meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, so let's start with why Owen found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class.
You're clearly a brilliant lawyer, and I really respect how hard you fight for Owen.
Don't manage me, Hale. You haven't answered my question: who decided on the zero, and was anyone told before it went into the gradebook?
Can you step out of the role and tell me how I should handle this?
You're asking me how to do your job? Withdraw the zero, Hale, and then tell me who decided it.
I just want us to be on the same team here.
Then why are we here, Hale? A team doesn't enter a zero first and call the parent after. Who decided it?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that Owen get an apology, and that you tell me in writing who decided to enter it before anyone called me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on who decided it, with the principal next.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "tell me how I should handle this", because asking her to do your job made her respect you less.
Try next time: at the very start, answer her question about Owen finding out from his phone by owning in one sentence that the zero went in before you called, instead of opening with a compliment.
